proposal.title: Anchor-Calibrated Mask-Channel Gating for HistGradientBoosting under Missingness Shift
proposal.hypothesis: When the shifted mechanism makes missingness itself carry label information that changes across domains (own-value MNAR, its reversal, grouped blocks), a predictor whose dependence on mask indicators is restricted to what is stable across training-simulated mechanisms will beat native-NaN HGB and random-mask augmentation on held-out mean AP, at no more than 0.01 AP clean loss.
proposal.mechanism: Native-NaN trees learn split directions for missing values, so P(y|x_obs,M) absorbs training-specific mask-label coupling. Under non-ignorable shift the Bayes predictor changes (atom_42235e794c05a946), and disregarding informative missingness helped most when that missingness was highly informative (atom_a7b4cd2b88c13161). We separate a value pathway from a mask pathway. Missing entries in the value pathway are filled by posterior draws conditioned on the anchors rather than a single plug-in value (atom_dbcde51203d2be87). The mask pathway is scored for cross-mechanism stability, and only features with stable mask effects keep a mask channel at inference.

proposed_primitives.definition: For each feature j, compare the change in validation log-loss from permuting mask column j across the four validation mechanisms. Keep the mask channel only if its sign and size are consistent (coefficient of variation below a threshold). Otherwise remove column j's mask channel and route j through the value pathway only.
K=5 draws of missing values from a Gaussian conditional fit on observed pairs, conditioned on anchors 0 and 1. The fit uses training rows only. Predictions are averaged over the draws.

relations.counterfactual_prediction: Without the gate, held-out MNAR AP drops toward the native-NaN baseline.
Using a single conditional mean worsens Brier score but leaves AP roughly unchanged.
Without augmentation, the gate estimates are noisy and select near-random features.

assumptions: The label-relevant structure of the clean values is the same in train and target; only missingness shifts.
The anchors are always observed and predict the informative features well.
Mask effects that are stable across MCAR20, MCAR40 and anchor-MAR proxy those that would be stable under the held-out mechanisms. This is unverifiable in general.
No target-batch statistics are used. If an optional variant is run, it uses only target mask rates.
strongest_prior_art: arxiv:2507.08280 (MIRRAMS): same goal of robustness to unseen missingness shift via label-relevant information. It uses mutual-information conditions rather than explicit per-feature mask gating with trees.
2406.16484v1: shows that dropping mask information helps under informative shift. It drops all mask information; we select features.
2106.00311v2: impute-then-regress is Bayes optimal within a fixed mechanism, but this does not address shift.
algorithm: 1. Split 60/20/20 with a fixed seed. Fit the anchor-conditional Gaussian on observed training pairs only.
2. Augment training data: add MCAR at 0-40% plus anchor-MAR masks on top of the observed masks. New masks are applied only to entries already observed.
3. Build a value view from K multidraw fills and a mask view from indicator columns.
4. Fit HGB on value view plus mask view, without scaling (trees ignore scaling, so there is no weight/scaler cancellation).
5. Score each mask channel by permutation on the four validation mechanisms and apply stable_mask_gate.
6. Refit with the ungated mask channels dropped. Tune hyperparameters on validation only.
7. At test time, predict as the average over K draws using observed values and masks only.
8. Report mean AP, Brier score and clean AP on the held-out mechanisms.
proposal.baseline: Native-NaN HistGradientBoosting; the same model plus random-mask augmentation; MIRRAMS-style MI-regularized MLP as the strongest constituent method.
ablations: Gate with a random feature subset of the same size.
Unconditional mean fill instead of anchor-conditional fill.
Matched tree budget and seeds (10 seeds) across all arms.
proposal.metric: Primary: mean AP averaged over the three held-out mechanisms. Secondary: Brier score and clean-test AP.
proposal.falsification: Reject the hypothesis if the full method's held-out mean AP is not at least 0.01 above the better of the two HGB baselines in paired seeds (95% CI excludes 0). Also reject if the random-subset gate matches the stable gate, or if clean AP drops by more than 0.01. Expected failure case: grouped structural missingness of features that the anchors do not predict, or MNAR where the reversal flips a mask effect that looked stable in validation.
proposal.feasibility: With 5000×20 data, K=5 and HGB, the expected cost is under 1 minute per seed on a CPU. No held-out labels are used for development.
